# Hosting and background services

- HST-001: Services with a scoped or transient lifetime should not be auto-activated, and auto-activated services should complete their initialization quickly to avoid delaying application startup; for longer-running initialization, consider background services or hosted services.
- HST-002: Don't cache an HttpClient that IHttpClientFactory created for a long time, and don't inject a typed client into a singleton service; consider requesting a client from IHttpClientFactory in a timely manner or each time you need one. Don't cache scope-related information (such as data from HttpContext) inside HttpMessageHandler instances or their dependencies. Don't register a typed client separately, because AddHttpClient already registers it. Don't start a large number of HTTP/1.1 requests at once without specifying limits.
- HST-003: Using the fully qualified name of the class that creates a log message as its category name is the recommended practice; in most cases, you should use log message template formatting when logging; and if a logging data store is slow, don't write to it directly.
- HST-004: AddDistributedMemoryCache should only be used in development or testing scenarios; it isn't a viable production implementation of IDistributedCache.
- HST-005: In a library that isn't an official Microsoft package, don't use the Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection namespace, and don't give its service registration extension methods names that are already part of the .NET ecosystem from official Microsoft packages.
